gospel.text:
[[Mc 10,1]]Jesus came into the district of Judea and across the Jordan. Again crowds gathered around him and, as was his custom, he again taught them.
[[Mc 10,2]]The Pharisees approached and asked, "Is it lawful for a husband to divorce his wife?" They were testing him.
[[Mc 10,3]]He said to them in reply, "What did Moses command you?"
[[Mc 10,4]]They replied, "Moses permitted him to write a bill of divorce and dismiss her."
[[Mc 10,5]]But Jesus told them, "Because of the hardness of your hearts he wrote you this commandment.
[[Mc 10,6]]But from the beginning of creation, 'God made them male and female.
[[Mc 10,7]]For this reason a man shall leave his father and mother (and be joined to his wife),
[[Mc 10,8]]and the two shall become one flesh.' So they are no longer two but one flesh.
[[Mc 10,9]]Therefore what God has joined together, no human being must separate."
[[Mc 10,10]]In the house the disciples again questioned him about this.
[[Mc 10,11]]He said to them, "Whoever divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery against her;
[[Mc 10,12]]and if she divorces her husband and marries another, she commits adultery."
gospel.title: Holy Gospel of Jesus Christ according to Saint Mark

psalm.title: Psalms
psalm.text:
[[Ps 119,12]]Blessed are you, O LORD; 
teach me your statutes.
[[Ps 119,16]]In your statutes I will delight; 
I will not forget your words.

[[Ps 119,18]]Open my eyes, that I may consider 
the wonders of your law.
[[Ps 119,27]]Make me understand the way of your precepts, 
and I will meditate on your wondrous deeds.

[[Ps 119,34]]Give me discernment, that I may observe your law 
and keep it with all my heart.
[[Ps 119,35]]Lead me in the path of your commands, 
for in it I delight.

first_reading.title: Book of Sirach
first_reading.text:
[[Si 6,5]]A kind mouth multiplies friends and appeases enemies, and gracious lips prompt friendly greetings.
[[Si 6,6]]Let your acquaintances be many, but one in a thousand your confidant.
[[Si 6,7]]When you gain a friend, first test him, and be not too ready to trust him
[[Si 6,8]]For one sort of friend is a friend when it suits him, but he will not be with you in time of distress.
[[Si 6,9]]Another is a friend who becomes an enemy, and tells of the quarrel to your shame.
[[Si 6,10]]Another is a friend, a boon companion, who will not be with you when sorrow comes.
[[Si 6,11]]When things go well, he is your other self, and lords it over your servants;
[[Si 6,12]]But if you are brought low, he turns against you and avoids meeting you.
[[Si 6,13]]Keep away from your enemies; be on your guard with your friends.
[[Si 6,14]]A faithful friend is a sturdy shelter; he who finds one finds a treasure.
[[Si 6,15]]A faithful friend is beyond price, no sum can balance his worth.
[[Si 6,16]]A faithful friend is a life-saving remedy, such as he who fears God finds;
[[Si 6,17]]For he who fears God behaves accordingly, and his friend will be like himself.
